tests.title: Common.Register adds a boolean --schema flag defaulting to false
given: a fresh Common and a new flag.FlagSet
tests.when: Common.Register(fs) is called
then: fs.Lookup("schema") is non-nil
its DefValue is "false"
its Value implements flag.Getter and Get() returns bool
tests.pseudocode: var c Common; fs := flag.NewFlagSet("t", flag.ContinueOnError); c.Register(fs); f := fs.Lookup("schema"); assert f != nil; assert f.DefValue == "false"

tests.title: Invoking a tool with --schema builds and prints the self-description document and exits 0
given: an App configured like fix, with Flags, Description, InputDescription, ExitCodes and ResultSample set
tests.when: app.Main is called with argv ["--schema"]
then: the returned exit code is 0
stdout is exactly one JSON object followed by a single trailing newline
the object has a top-level "tool" key
tests.pseudocode: code := app.Main(ctx, []string{"--schema"}, stdin, &stdout, &stderr); assert code == 0; assert json.Unmarshal(stdout.Bytes(), &m) == nil; assert bytes.HasSuffix(stdout.Bytes(), []byte("}\n"))

tests.title: --version keeps priority over --schema when both are given
given: an App named "tool" with Version "9.9.9"
tests.when: app.Main is called with argv ["--schema", "--version"]
then: stdout is exactly "tool 9.9.9\n"
the exit code is 0
the self-description document is not printed
tests.pseudocode: code := app.Main(ctx, []string{"--schema","--version"}, stdin, &stdout, &stderr); assert stdout.String() == "tool 9.9.9\n"; assert code == 0

tests.title: --schema alongside --output, --events and --events-file creates no files and has no run
given: a temp directory with no pre-existing files named out.json, events.json or ev2.json
tests.when: the fix binary is run with ["--schema", "--output", "out.json", "--events", "events.json", "--events-file", "ev2.json"]
then: the process exits 0
none of out.json, events.json or ev2.json exist afterward
stdout carries only the self-description document
tests.pseudocode: run(bin, "--schema","--output",tmp+"/out.json","--events",tmp+"/events.json","--events-file",tmp+"/ev2.json"); assert !exists(tmp+"/out.json"); assert !exists(tmp+"/events.json"); assert !exists(tmp+"/ev2.json")

tests.title: A positional argument given alongside --schema is accepted and ignored
given: the fix binary built once for both invocations
tests.when: fix is run once as ["--schema"] and once as ["--schema", "some text"]
then: the two invocations' stdout byte sequences are identical
tests.pseudocode: a := run(bin, "--schema"); b := run(bin, "--schema", "some text"); assert a.stdout == b.stdout; assert a.exitCode == b.exitCode

tests.title: An unparseable flag given alongside --schema reports flag.Parse's own error, not the document
given: the fix binary
tests.when: fix is run with ["--schema", "--not-a-real-flag"]
then: the exit code is 2
stderr contains flag.Parse's own "flag provided but not defined" style message
stdout does not contain a top-level "flags" key
tests.pseudocode: r := run(bin, "--schema", "--not-a-real-flag"); assert r.exitCode == 2; assert strings.Contains(r.stderr, "flag provided but not defined"); assert !strings.Contains(r.stdout, "\"flags\"")

tests.title: --schema exits 0 with no credential configured, --dir an empty directory, and no network reachable
given: no AF_MODEL, AGENTKIT_MODEL, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, OPENAI_API_KEY, GITHUB_TOKEN or GITLAB_TOKEN set
--dir points at a freshly created, empty temp directory
the default HTTP transport is replaced with one that fails any dial
tests.when: each of spec, issue, fix, and impl is run with ["--dir", emptyDir, "--schema"]
then: every invocation exits 0
the self-description document is printed for each
no outbound connection attempt is observed
no credential or model-resolution error appears in stderr
tests.pseudocode: for tool in [spec,issue,fix,impl]: r := run(bin(tool), "--dir", emptyDir, "--schema"); assert r.exitCode == 0; assert !dialAttempted; assert !strings.Contains(r.stderr, "credential")

tests.title: The self-description document carries exactly the seven top-level keys, with tool and schema_version matching an ordinary envelope
given: fix built as a binary
tests.when: fix is run once with ["--schema"] and once with ["--land", "bogus", "text"] (a usage error that still emits an envelope without resolving a model)
then: the --schema document's top-level keys are exactly {tool, schema_version, description, input, flags, result, exit_codes}
the document's tool field equals the usage-error envelope's tool field
the document's schema_version field equals the usage-error envelope's schema_version field
tests.pseudocode: doc := parse(run(bin,"--schema").stdout); env := parse(run(bin,"--land","bogus","text").stdout); assert set(doc.keys()) == {tool,schema_version,description,input,flags,result,exit_codes}; assert doc.tool == env.tool; assert doc.schema_version == env.schema_version

tests.title: Each tool's description field is its own hand-authored one-sentence value
given: spec, issue, fix and impl each built as binaries
tests.when: each is run with ["--schema"]
then: each document's description is a non-empty single sentence with no embedded newline
the four descriptions are pairwise distinct
tests.pseudocode: descs := {}; for tool in [spec,issue,fix,impl]: d := parse(run(bin(tool),"--schema").stdout).description; assert d != "" && !strings.Contains(d,"\n"); descs[tool]=d; assert len(set(descs.values())) == 4

tests.title: Every tool's input field carries the same closed four-element kinds list regardless of what that tool's CheckInput refuses
given: spec, issue, fix and impl each built as binaries
impl's own CheckInput refuses the issue kind at runtime
tests.when: each is run with ["--schema"]
then: each document's input.kinds equals exactly ["text","file","stdin","issue"]
each document's input.description is a non-empty string
impl's input.kinds still includes "issue" even though impl refuses issue input on an ordinary run
tests.pseudocode: for tool in [spec,issue,fix,impl]: d := parse(run(bin(tool),"--schema").stdout); assert d.input.kinds == ["text","file","stdin","issue"]; assert d.input.description != ""

tests.title: A tool's exit_codes lists exactly the codes its Exec can actually return, each with a hand-authored description
given: fix built as a binary, whose Exec can return 0, 1, 2, 3 and 4
tests.when: fix is run with ["--schema"]
then: the document's exit_codes has keys "0","1","2","3","4" and no others
every value is a non-empty one-line string
tests.pseudocode: d := parse(run(fixBin,"--schema").stdout); assert set(d.exit_codes.keys()) == {0,1,2,3,4}; for v in d.exit_codes.values(): assert v != "" && !strings.Contains(v,"\n")

tests.title: issue and spec each report exactly three exit codes: 0, 1 and 2
given: issue and spec each built as binaries
tests.when: each is run with ["--schema"]
then: each document's exit_codes has exactly the keys "0", "1" and "2"
tests.pseudocode: for tool in [issue,spec]: d := parse(run(bin(tool),"--schema").stdout); assert set(d.exit_codes.keys()) == {0,1,2}

tests.title: fix and impl each report exactly five exit codes: 0 through 4
given: fix and impl each built as binaries
tests.when: each is run with ["--schema"]
then: each document's exit_codes has exactly the keys "0","1","2","3","4"
tests.pseudocode: for tool in [fix,impl]: d := parse(run(bin(tool),"--schema").stdout); assert set(d.exit_codes.keys()) == {0,1,2,3,4}

tests.title: The flags document's property order follows fs.VisitAll's stable name order over Common plus the tool's own flags
given: a FlagSet with Common's flags registered, then two tool-specific flags "zeta" and "alpha" registered via the tool's Flags closure
tests.when: the flags generator walks the FlagSet
then: the generated properties appear in the same order fs.VisitAll would visit them, lexicographic by flag name
tests.pseudocode: var names []string; fs.VisitAll(func(f *flag.Flag){names=append(names,f.Name)}); doc := flagsSchema(fs); assert orderOf(doc.properties, excluding(schema,version)) == filter(names, excluding(schema,version))

tests.title: The flags document excludes the schema and version flags themselves
given: a FlagSet carrying --schema and --version among other flags
tests.when: the flags generator builds the document
then: flags.properties has no key named "schema"
flags.properties has no key named "version"
tests.pseudocode: doc := flagsSchema(fs); _, hasSchema := doc.properties["schema"]; _, hasVersion := doc.properties["version"]; assert !hasSchema && !hasVersion

tests.title: A flag's description is its Usage string verbatim
given: a FlagSet with a flag registered with Usage "the exact usage text"
tests.when: the flags generator builds the document
then: that property's description equals "the exact usage text" exactly, unmodified
tests.pseudocode: fs.StringVar(&v,"x","","the exact usage text"); doc := flagsSchema(fs); assert doc.properties["x"].description == "the exact usage text"

tests.title: A flag registered through StringVar, BoolVar, IntVar or Float64Var reports the JSON type matching its Getter's dynamic type
tests.when: for any flag registered via StringVar, BoolVar, IntVar, or Float64Var with an arbitrary default value
then: the generated property's type is "string" for StringVar, "boolean" for BoolVar, "integer" for IntVar, and "number" for Float64Var
the generated property's default equals the flag's own default value
tests.pseudocode: for (register,def,wantType) in [(StringVar,"x",string),(BoolVar,true,boolean),(IntVar,7,integer),(Float64Var,3.14,number)]: fs := flag.NewFlagSet(...); register(&v,"f",def,"u"); doc := flagsSchema(fs); assert doc.properties["f"].type == wantType; assert doc.properties["f"].default == def

tests.title: A time.Duration flag renders as a string with format duration, default in the duration's own string form
given: a FlagSet with fs.DurationVar(&v, "verify-timeout", 10*time.Minute, "...") registered
tests.when: the flags generator builds the document
then: flags.properties["verify-timeout"] equals {type: string, format: duration, default: "10m0s", description: "..."}
tests.pseudocode: fs.DurationVar(&v,"verify-timeout",10*time.Minute,"..."); doc := flagsSchema(fs); p := doc.properties["verify-timeout"]; assert p.type == "string" && p.format == "duration" && p.default == "10m0s"

tests.title: fix's hand-written --pull flag, which does not implement flag.Getter, is reported as a plain string using its own String()
given: the fully-populated FlagSet fix's App.Main constructs, including --pull registered via fs.Var(&pull, "pull", theUsageString)
tests.when: the flags generator builds fix's flags document
then: flags.properties["pull"] equals {type: string, default: pull.String(), description: theUsageString}
tests.pseudocode: doc := flagsSchema(fixFlagSet); p := doc.properties["pull"]; assert p.type == "string"; assert p.default == (&pullFlag{}).String(); assert p.description == theUsageString

tests.title: A flag declared with a closed set of legal values carries an enum key listing exactly that set
given: fix's --land flag, declared alongside its StringVar with the enum ["pr","branch","none"]
fix's --repo flag, which takes free text and has no such declaration
tests.when: the flags generator builds fix's flags document
then: flags.properties["land"].enum equals ["pr","branch","none"]
flags.properties["repo"] carries no enum key
tests.pseudocode: doc := flagsSchema(fixFlagSet); assert doc.properties["land"].enum == ["pr","branch","none"]; _, hasEnum := doc.properties["repo"]["enum"]; assert !hasEnum

tests.title: The flags document is shaped as a standalone object schema with no required or additionalProperties keys
given: any populated FlagSet
tests.when: the flags generator builds the document
then: the top-level shape is {$schema: the 2020-12 meta-schema URI, type: object, properties: {...}}
there is no "required" key
there is no "additionalProperties" key
tests.pseudocode: doc := flagsSchema(fs); assert doc["$schema"] == "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema"; assert doc["type"] == "object"; _, hasReq := doc["required"]; _, hasAP := doc["additionalProperties"]; assert !hasReq && !hasAP

tests.title: A struct type renders as an object schema whose property order follows reflect.VisibleFields, including promoted embedded fields
given: specgen.Result, which embeds Package anonymously
tests.when: the result generator renders reflect.TypeOf(specgen.Result{})
then: the schema's type is "object"
the properties order matches reflect.VisibleFields(reflect.TypeOf(specgen.Result{})) filtered to exported JSON fields
Package's own fields appear in place, promoted, not nested under a "Package" key
tests.pseudocode: s := resultSchema(reflect.TypeOf(specgen.Result{})); assert s.type == "object"; assert orderOf(s.properties) == jsonFieldOrder(reflect.VisibleFields(reflect.TypeOf(specgen.Result{})))

tests.title: A field's JSON name and required-ness follow its json tag exactly as encoding/json reads it
given: a struct with a field tagged json:"a" with no omitempty, one tagged json:"b,omitempty", and one tagged json:"-"
tests.when: the result generator renders that struct type
then: properties contains "a" and "required" includes "a"
properties contains "b" and "required" does not include "b"
properties does not contain a key for the field tagged json:"-"
tests.pseudocode: type T struct{ A string `json:"a"`; B string `json:"b,omitempty"`; C string `json:"-"` }; s := resultSchema(reflect.TypeOf(T{})); assert contains(s.required,"a") && !contains(s.required,"b"); assert !hasKey(s.properties,"c")

tests.title: A slice field, a pointer field and a scalar field each render as the expected JSON Schema node
given: a struct with a []string field, a *SubStruct field, and an int field
tests.when: the result generator renders that struct type
then: the slice field's schema is {type: array, items: {type: string}}
the pointer field's schema equals SubStruct's own object schema with no nullable marker of any kind
the int field's schema is {type: integer}
tests.pseudocode: type Sub struct{ N int `json:"n"` }; type T struct{ L []string `json:"l"`; P *Sub `json:"p"`; I int `json:"i"` }; s := resultSchema(reflect.TypeOf(T{})); assert s.properties["l"] == {type:array,items:{type:string}}; assert s.properties["p"] == resultSchema(reflect.TypeOf(Sub{})); assert s.properties["i"] == {type:integer}

tests.title: Every field reachable from toolio.Envelope and from a tool's Result type carries a description sourced from the new struct tag
given: toolio.Envelope and codefix.Result, both fully tagged as this scope requires
tests.when: the result generator renders reflect.TypeOf(toolio.Envelope{}) and reflect.TypeOf(codefix.Result{})
then: every generated property carries a non-empty "description" string
each description equals the value of that field's description struct tag, not its json tag or Go doc comment
tests.pseudocode: for typ in [reflect.TypeOf(toolio.Envelope{}), reflect.TypeOf(codefix.Result{})]: s := resultSchema(typ); walk(s.properties, func(name,node){ assert node.description != "" })

tests.title: An object schema's properties marshal in declaration order, not Go map key order
given: a struct type whose declared field order is z, a, m, deliberately not alphabetical
tests.when: the generated schema is marshalled to JSON
then: the raw JSON's "properties" object lists keys in the order z, a, m, not alphabetically sorted
tests.pseudocode: type T struct{ Z int `json:"z"`; A int `json:"a"`; M int `json:"m"` }; s := resultSchema(reflect.TypeOf(T{})); b,_ := json.Marshal(s); assert rawKeyOrder(b,"properties") == ["z","a","m"]

tests.title: The envelope's Result field is substituted with the schema of the running tool's own concrete Result type
given: an App with ResultSample set to a zero-value codefix.Result{}
tests.when: the result document is built for that App from toolio.Envelope
then: result.properties.result equals the object schema generated directly from codefix.Result, not a generic {type: object} placeholder
tests.pseudocode: doc := resultDocumentFor(app); assert doc.properties["result"] == resultSchema(reflect.TypeOf(codefix.Result{}))

tests.title: The result document is a standalone, independently valid JSON Schema 2020-12 document
given: an App configured with a ResultSample
tests.when: the result document is built
then: its top-level shape is {$schema: the 2020-12 meta-schema URI, type: object, properties: {...}, required: [...]}
it carries no reference to the flags document
tests.pseudocode: doc := resultDocumentFor(app); assert doc["$schema"] == "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema"; assert doc["type"]=="object"; _, hasProps := doc["properties"]; _, hasReq := doc["required"]; assert hasProps && hasReq

tests.title: Envelope.SchemaVersion is tagged json:"schema_version", sits immediately after Version, and is never omitted
given: the toolio.Envelope struct definition
tests.when: reflect.VisibleFields(reflect.TypeOf(toolio.Envelope{})) is inspected, and an Envelope with a zero-value SchemaVersion is marshalled
then: the field named SchemaVersion has json tag "schema_version" with no omitempty option
it occupies the index immediately after the Version field
marshalling an Envelope always yields a "schema_version" key, even when its value is the empty string
tests.pseudocode: fields := reflect.VisibleFields(reflect.TypeOf(toolio.Envelope{})); assert fields[indexOf("Version")+1].Name == "SchemaVersion"; tag := fields[indexOf("SchemaVersion")].Tag.Get("json"); assert tag == "schema_version"; b,_ := json.Marshal(toolio.Envelope{}); assert strings.Contains(string(b),"schema_version")

tests.title: All four tools set Envelope.SchemaVersion from the same shared constant
given: spec, issue, fix and impl each built as binaries
tests.when: each is run to produce an ordinary envelope via a usage error that still calls Run.Envelope, e.g. an invalid --land value on fix/impl, an invalid --repo on issue/spec
then: all four envelopes' schema_version fields are identical
that value equals toolio.SchemaVersion
tests.pseudocode: vals := {}; for tool in [spec,issue,fix,impl]: env := parse(runUsageError(bin(tool)).stdout); vals[tool]=env.schema_version; assert len(set(vals.values()))==1; assert vals["fix"] == toolio.SchemaVersion

tests.title: toolio.SchemaVersion is the literal string 2.0.0
tests.when: toolio.SchemaVersion is read
then: its value is exactly "2.0.0"
tests.pseudocode: assert toolio.SchemaVersion == "2.0.0"

tests.title: The run_start progress event carries schema_version under the same key as the envelope
given: a run configured with an events sink per 07_progress_event_stream, driven end to end with a scripted model
tests.when: the run completes and its emitted events are captured
then: the run_start event's JSON object has a "schema_version" key
its value equals toolio.SchemaVersion
tests.pseudocode: events := runWithEventsSink(...); rs := findEvent(events,"run_start"); assert rs["schema_version"] == toolio.SchemaVersion

tests.title: The written compatibility rule classifies the four named kinds of envelope change as additive
given: docs/adr/06-version-the-envelope-interface.md
tests.when: the ADR's decision section is read
then: it names, as additive: a new top-level field, a new field on an existing object such as result/needs_human/error/a warning/an event, a new value in a field documented as an open set, and a new event type
tests.pseudocode: text := readFile("docs/adr/06-version-the-envelope-interface.md"); for phrase in ["new top-level","new field on an existing object","open set","new event type"]: assert strings.Contains(text,phrase)

tests.title: The written compatibility rule classifies removal, renaming, type change and enum narrowing as breaking
given: docs/adr/06-version-the-envelope-interface.md
tests.when: the ADR's decision section is read
then: it names, as breaking: removing a field, renaming a field, changing a field's type, and narrowing a field documented as a closed enum
it states each of these bumps the major version
tests.pseudocode: text := readFile("docs/adr/06-version-the-envelope-interface.md"); for phrase in ["removing","renaming","changing a field's type","narrowing","major"]: assert strings.Contains(text,phrase)

tests.title: Each tool ships a checked-in golden file holding its --schema output's exact bytes
given: cmd/spec/testdata/schema.golden.json, cmd/issue/testdata/schema.golden.json, cmd/fix/testdata/schema.golden.json and cmd/impl/testdata/schema.golden.json exist in the repository
tests.when: each tool is built and run with ["--schema"]
then: the live stdout bytes equal the corresponding golden file's bytes exactly, for every one of the four tools
tests.pseudocode: for tool in [spec,issue,fix,impl]: live := run(bin(tool),"--schema").stdout; golden := readFile("cmd/"+tool+"/testdata/schema.golden.json"); assert live == golden

tests.title: A drifted golden file fails the golden-file test with a byte-level diff naming the tool
given: a copy of cmd/fix/testdata/schema.golden.json mutated to differ from fix's live --schema output
tests.when: the golden-file test in cmd/fix is run, e.g. `go test -run TestSchemaGolden ./cmd/fix`, against the mutated file
then: the test run exits non-zero
its output names "fix" and shows a diff between the live and golden bytes
tests.pseudocode: mutate("cmd/fix/testdata/schema.golden.json"); out, code := exec("go","test","-run","TestSchemaGolden","./cmd/fix"); assert code != 0; assert strings.Contains(out,"fix"); assert strings.Contains(out,"diff") || strings.Contains(out,"-"); restoreOriginal()

tests.title: The golden-file update path regenerates the golden file instead of failing
given: a copy of cmd/fix/testdata/schema.golden.json mutated to differ from fix's live --schema output
tests.when: the golden-file test is run with its update path set, e.g. `UPDATE_GOLDEN=1 go test -run TestSchemaGolden ./cmd/fix`
then: the test run exits 0
the golden file's bytes afterward equal the live --schema output
tests.pseudocode: mutate("cmd/fix/testdata/schema.golden.json"); out, code := execWithEnv({UPDATE_GOLDEN:"1"},"go","test","-run","TestSchemaGolden","./cmd/fix"); assert code == 0; assert readFile("cmd/fix/testdata/schema.golden.json") == run(fixBin,"--schema").stdout

tests.title: Both flags and result of every tool's --schema output compile against the JSON Schema 2020-12 meta-schema
given: spec, issue, fix and impl each built as binaries
github.com/santhosh-tekuri/jsonschema/v6 loaded with the 2020-12 meta-schema
tests.when: each tool's --schema output is parsed and its flags and result values are compiled as schemas
then: compilation succeeds for both flags and result, for all four tools
a deliberately invalid document, e.g. one missing "type", fails compilation, proving the check is not a no-op
tests.pseudocode: compiler := jsonschema.NewCompiler(); for tool in [spec,issue,fix,impl]: doc := parse(run(bin(tool),"--schema").stdout); assert compiles(compiler,doc.flags); assert compiles(compiler,doc.result); assert !compiles(compiler,{properties:{}})

tests.title: The exhaustiveness checker names every field reachable from a type that lacks the description tag
given: a synthetic struct type with one tagged field (description present) and one untagged field
toolio.Envelope and each of the four Result types, all fully tagged
tests.when: the exhaustiveness checker walks the synthetic type, and separately walks toolio.Envelope and the four Result types
then: walking the synthetic type reports exactly one missing field, named by its Go field name
walking toolio.Envelope and each Result type reports no missing fields
tests.pseudocode: type Bad struct{ A string `json:"a" description:"has one"`; B string `json:"b"` }; missing := checkDescriptions(reflect.TypeOf(Bad{})); assert missing == ["B"]; for typ in [toolio.Envelope{},codefix.Result{},codeimpl.Result{},issuetriage.Result{},specgen.Result{}]: assert checkDescriptions(reflect.TypeOf(typ)) == nil

tests.title: docs/cli.md's shared-flags table has a --schema row describing its default and effect
given: docs/cli.md

the row states its default is false and describes that it prints the self-description document instead of running

tests.title: docs/cli.md has a Self-description (--schema) section with a worked example and an explanation of flags, result and exit_codes

tests.title: docs/cli.md has an Interface versions section listing 1.0.0 and 2.0.0 with the additive/breaking rule
given: docs/cli.md
tests.when: the document is scanned for a heading matching "Interface versions"
then: the section exists

tests.title: The ADR docs/adr/06-version-the-envelope-interface.md records context, decision and consequence as an accepted decision

tests.when: docs/adr/06-version-the-envelope-interface.md is read

tests.title: A caller introspects fix's interface with no credential configured before ever running it
given: fix built as a real binary
no model credential environment variable set
--dir points at a freshly created, empty directory
the meta-schema for JSON Schema 2020-12 is available to the caller
tests.when: the caller runs 'fix --dir <empty-dir> --schema'
then: fix exits 0
stdout is exactly one JSON document carrying tool, schema_version, description, input, flags, result and exit_codes
the document's flags and result both compile against the 2020-12 meta-schema
no network connection was attempted and no model was resolved

tests.title: A maintainer's undeclared Result field change is caught by the golden-file test
given: a working copy of the repository with codefix.Result temporarily given one new exported, tagged field
cmd/fix/testdata/schema.golden.json left unchanged

tests.title: An ordinary run of issue reports the same schema_version its own --schema advertised
given: issue built as a real binary
a valid issue report as input
a scripted model provider standing in for the real vendor
tests.when: the caller first runs 'issue --schema' and records schema_version, then runs 'issue' on a real report to completion
then: the ordinary run's envelope carries schema_version "2.0.0", identical to the value '--schema' advertised
the caller's equality check between the two values succeeds
